simple.meaning: מוּצַק (mûwtsaq) is a Hebrew word meaning “narrowness ; figuratively, distress.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: מוּצַק (H4164) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Job 36:16, with occurrences in Job, Isaiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מוּצַק (H4164) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in מוּצַק (H4164) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: מוּצַק (mûwtsaq) / H4164 is traced through Job 36:16, Job 37:10, Isaiah 8:23 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H4164. mutsaq II. מוּצָק מוּצָק, noun [masculine] constraint, distress ; — absolute מוּצָק Isaiah 8:23 distress ; absolute also מוּצָק Job 36:16 , of distress as constraint (opposed to רַחַב ); בְּמוּצָ֑ק מַיִם רֹחַב 37:10 , literally in constraint (i.e. frozen). — 1. מוּצָק see יצק .

occurrences.englishText: Yes, he would have allured you out of distress,
By the breath of God, ice is given,
